understand:
After an assessment, your dentist takes scans or impressions and plans the movement of your teeth. A series of custom aligners is made, and you change to the next set as directed. You’ll have regular reviews to check progress.

Aligners only work while they’re in your mouth. They need to be worn for most of the day and night, taken out only to eat, drink anything other than water, and clean your teeth.

benefits: No brackets or wires to irritate the mouth
Easier to brush and floss than with fixed braces
consider: Results depend on wearing the aligners as directed
Not suitable for every type of tooth movement
You’ll need a retainer afterwards, possibly long term

care: Rinse and gently clean your aligners when you take them out, and brush your teeth before putting them back in.
Take aligners out to eat and for drinks other than water.
Keep them in their case when they’re out, so they aren’t lost or damaged.
faqs: Only an assessment can tell. Some people are better suited to fixed braces or an orthodontist, and your dentist will be upfront about it.
Many people feel pressure or tightness for a day or two after changing to a new set. This usually settles.
How long will I need a retainer?
Teeth tend to drift back after treatment. Your dentist will recommend a retainer plan to hold the result.
